paragraphs: On Thursday, Leo gave a talk to the Explorers in the school library. The title was "Three Fun Ways to Keep Fit." He wore a small green badge, and he held a small card. Mia held the camera, and May sat in the front row. The room was quiet, and Leo took a deep breath. "Exercise is good for you," he said. "It makes your body strong, and it makes you happy." "Today I will give you three examples."

"My first example is cycling," said Leo. "You can cycle to school, or you can cycle in the park." "My friend Tom cycles to school every day, and he is very fit." "Tom is thirteen, and he is in the secondary part of our school." "A good cycling helmet is important, and you must use it." Mia asked, "Is it good for the legs?" "Yes, it is good for the legs and for the heart," said Leo.

"My second example is dancing," said Leo. "There are classes for a beginner and for an advanced dancer." "The beginner class is on Saturday morning at the sports center." "The advanced class is in the afternoon." "A TV celebrity dances for ten minutes every morning, and she says that it is fun." Leo put his card down and moved his arms. Everybody laughed, and May clapped her hands. "You do not need a big space," he said. "You can dance in your room."

"My third example is football," said Leo. "It is a team game, and you meet new friends." "Each player has a job, and the game is never boring." "Coach Matt has a football practice on Tuesday and Friday." "Among all the sports, football is my favorite." "That is only my opinion, and it is not a fact," he said with a smile. Lily wrote "cycling, dancing, football" in her notebook.

"Where can we find the latest news?" asked Lily. "On the school site," said Leo. "The Sports page has a list of all the classes and all the times." Teacher Kim said, "Thank you, Leo, this was a very good talk." "You gave three clear examples, and you spoke slowly." Leo smiled, and for once he did not say anything funny. Lily wrote a title for the blog: "Three Fun Ways to Keep Fit."

sentences.text: On Thursday, Leo gave a talk to the Explorers in the school library.
The title was "Three Fun Ways to Keep Fit."
He wore a small green badge, and he held a small card.
Mia held the camera, and May sat in the front row.
The room was quiet, and Leo took a deep breath.
"Exercise is good for you," he said.
"It makes your body strong, and it makes you happy."
"Today I will give you three examples."
"My first example is cycling," said Leo.
"You can cycle to school, or you can cycle in the park."
"My friend Tom cycles to school every day, and he is very fit."
"Tom is thirteen, and he is in the secondary part of our school."
"A good cycling helmet is important, and you must use it."
Mia asked, "Is it good for the legs?"
"Yes, it is good for the legs and for the heart," said Leo.
"My second example is dancing," said Leo.
"There are classes for a beginner and for an advanced dancer."
"The beginner class is on Saturday morning at the sports center."
"The advanced class is in the afternoon."
"A TV celebrity dances for ten minutes every morning, and she says that it is fun."
Leo put his card down and moved his arms.
Everybody laughed, and May clapped her hands.
"You do not need a big space," he said.
"You can dance in your room."
"My third example is football," said Leo.
"It is a team game, and you meet new friends."
"Each player has a job, and the game is never boring."
"Coach Matt has a football practice on Tuesday and Friday."
"Among all the sports, football is my favorite."
"That is only my opinion, and it is not a fact," he said with a smile.
Lily wrote "cycling, dancing, football" in her notebook.
"Where can we find the latest news?" asked Lily.
"On the school site," said Leo.
"The Sports page has a list of all the classes and all the times."
Teacher Kim said, "Thank you, Leo, this was a very good talk."
"You gave three clear examples, and you spoke slowly."
Leo smiled, and for once he did not say anything funny.
Lily wrote a title for the blog: "Three Fun Ways to Keep Fit."
